$comment: Trusted text and String calls judged by both editors alike: a raw-string Trusted, and one given its text by name, html = ..., are read as the text they hold, in a call to interpolate, in a val set to one and in a Kotlin template; toString on any value is a String, and a String call after !! on a String? is a String too, while a safe call may be null.

cases.name: a raw-string Trusted origin fixes the host of a script src
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted("""https://cdn.example.com/"""), q)

cases.name: an empty raw-string Trusted fixes nothing
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted(""""""), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a raw-string Trusted tag name puts the value in code
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<%s>%s</%s>", Trusted("""script"""), q, Trusted("""script"""))

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in a script or style element, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a raw-string Trusted in a template is read as the markup it writes

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into onclick, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there.

cases.name: toString on any value is a String, refused in an expression
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(n: Long) = interpolate("""

""", n.toString())

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: n.toString() lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

cases.name: toString on any value is a String in a template

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${n.toString()} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(n: Long) = interpolate("

x

", n.toString()).text
